overall: The AG found the Phillipston Selectboard violated the Open Meeting Law on Nov. 18, 2020 by discussing an unnoticed topic and by failing to identify the specific property before entering executive session; it ordered future compliance and release of the executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Board discussed return of the elementary school building at its Nov. 18, 2020 meeting, a topic not on the posted notice.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the topic should have been included on the meeting notice or should not have been discussed until a future meeting when notice could be provided to the public.

allegations.summary: Chair did not identify the specific property to be discussed in the announcement before the Board entered executive session on Nov. 18, 2020.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if we accept that the Chair did not anticipate holding a discussion about the return of the school building in executive session and for that reason had not included the required level of detail on the meeting notice, the Board still violated the Law when the Chair failed to identify the specific property to be discussed in the announcement before entering executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release the minutes of the November 18 executive session in their entirety within 30 days of the letter date.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law. We further order the Board to publicly release the minutes of its November 18 executive session in their entirety within 30 days of the date of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
